month.name: month
month.description: In HSE analytics, 'month' refers to a calendar period of approximately 30 days used for tracking, reporting, and analyzing safety and environmental data. Monthly intervals are commonly used to identify trends, monitor compliance, and assess the frequency of incidents, near misses, or hazards over time. Observations and reports are often grouped by month to facilitate regular reviews and targeted interventions.
examples: Three near misses were reported in the month of April.
Monthly safety inspections were completed for all work areas.
There was a spike in environmental observations last month.
Monthly incident review identified recurring slip hazards.
No lost time injuries occurred during the month.

quarter.name: quarter
quarter.description: In the HSE context, 'quarter' denotes a three-month period used for summarizing and analyzing safety and environmental performance. Quarterly intervals help organizations track progress, compare trends, and evaluate the effectiveness of safety initiatives over a longer timeframe than monthly reviews. Reports and observations are often aggregated by quarter for management review and regulatory compliance.
examples: Quarterly incident rates decreased compared to the previous quarter.
Quarterly safety training was completed by all staff.
There were five environmental spills reported in Q2.
Quarterly review highlighted an increase in near misses.
No recordable injuries occurred during the last quarter.

year.name: year
year.description: In HSE analytics, 'year' refers to a twelve-month period used for comprehensive tracking and evaluation of safety and environmental performance. Annual intervals are essential for identifying long-term trends, setting targets, and fulfilling regulatory reporting requirements. Yearly summaries aggregate incidents, hazards, and observations to inform strategic planning and continuous improvement.
examples: The total number of recordable injuries decreased this year.
Annual safety audit was completed in December.
Yearly environmental compliance report was submitted.
There were no fatalities reported last year.
Year-to-date near miss count is lower than previous years.
